Add an Icon legend to a map

Source: R/layers.R
addIconLegend.Rd

Add an Icon legend to a map, either by manually specifying icons, labels, and colours, or by providing an icon scale function (from iconFactor(), iconBin() or iconQuantile()) in the same way as leaflet::addLegend(). Useful in conjunction with magicIcons() to communicate the meaning of icons/colours.

Usage

addIconLegend(
  map,
  icons,
  labels,
  colors = "black",
  title = NULL,
  library = "fontawesome",
  position = c("topright", "bottomright", "bottomleft", "topleft"),
  layerId = NULL,
  className = "info legend",
  data = leaflet::getMapData(map),
  pal,
  values,
  na.label = "NA",
  labFormat = leaflet::labelFormat(),
  opacity = 1,
  group = NULL
)

Arguments

map

a map widget object created from leaflet()

icons

Name of the icons, from the icon library defined by library. A full list of available icons can be found using fontawesome::fa_metadata(), https://icons.getbootstrap.com/, https://ionic.io/ionicons or https://lucide.dev/icons/. Should not be provided if pal is used.

labels

Labels for each icon; should be the same length as icons. Labels are inserted as HTML, so may contain formatting such as "PM<sub>2.5</sub>". If pal is used, labels are generated using labFormat, but can be overridden by providing labels.

colors

Colours to use for each icon. If length(colors) == 1L it is recycled for all icons. Otherwise should be the same length as icons. If pal is used, colors may also be a colour scale function, such as one created using leaflet::colorFactor(), leaflet::colorBin() or leaflet::colorQuantile().

title

the legend title; optional. If pal is used and values is a formula, the title defaults to the variable name in the formula, as in leaflet::addLegend().

library

One of "fontawesome", "bootstrap", "ionicons", or "lucide" defining the icon library of interest. Defaults to "fontawesome". Alternatively, "text" shows icon as text, which is useful for numbered or lettered markers (e.g., icon = 1:10). Text is bold and shrinks to fit, so is best kept to around three characters. "svg" uses icon as raw SVG markup (e.g., '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">...</svg>'), so any icon can be used. Parts of the SVG which use currentColor or have no fill of their own take on iconColor. Only use SVG markup you trust, as it is inserted directly into legends.

position

position of control: "topleft", "topright", "bottomleft", or "bottomright".

layerId

the layer id

className

extra CSS classes to append to the control, space separated

data

the data object from which the argument values are derived; by default, it is the data object provided to leaflet() initially, but can be overridden

pal

An icon scale function created using iconFactor(), iconBin() or iconQuantile(). If provided, icons should not be.

values

The values used to generate icons from pal. Either a vector or a formula to be evaluated against data (e.g., ~type). May be omitted for scales with a fixed domain or levels, except for iconQuantile() without a domain.

na.label

The legend label for missing values.

labFormat

A function to format the labels derived from pal and values. See leaflet::labelFormat().

opacity

The opacity of the legend icons, between 0 and 1. Note that this defaults to 1, rather than the 0.5 of leaflet::addLegend(), so that icons are shown in their true colours.

group

The group of a layer (e.g., the markers created using magicIcons()). If provided, the legend is shown/hidden alongside that group, e.g., using leaflet::addLayersControl(). In Shiny, using group with leaflet::leafletProxy() requires the original map to already contain a grouped icon legend.

Value

a leaflet widget

Using icon scales

Like leaflet::addLegend(), a legend can be generated automatically by passing an icon scale function to pal alongside the values used on the map. The icons and labels are then determined from the levels or bins of the scale, and labels are formatted using labFormat. For example, an iconBin() scale would be shown as one icon per bin, labelled with the range of that bin.

In this case colors may also be a colour scale function, such as one created using leaflet::colorBin() with the same settings as the icon scale, giving a legend of matched icon-colour pairs.

Legend items are derived exactly as in leaflet::addLegend(): factor scales show the sorted unique values, bin scales show one item per bin, and quantile scales show one item per quantile of values (with the quantile values in a hover tooltip). An icon legend and a colour legend built from scales with the same settings will therefore always agree. Unlike leaflet::addLegend(), values may be omitted when the scale has a fixed domain/levels, and iconBin() scales with no domain are supported. For the latter, the legend shows only the bins that contain values, with the same icons (and colours, if colors is a colour scale) as the map. Like leaflet::colorBin(), such a scale assigns icons based on which bins are occupied, so empty bins have no icon to show.

If any values are missing, an extra legend item is added using the na.icon of the scale and labelled with na.label. Its colour is the na.color of colors if it is a colour scale, and otherwise grey ("#808080", the default na.color in {leaflet}). As in leaflet::addLegend(), this is skipped if na.label is already one of the labels, if na.icon is NA, or if colors is a colour scale with a transparent na.color.

Examples

library(leaflet)
addIconLegend(
  map = leaflet(),
  icons = c("beer", "school"),
  labels = c("Pub", "University"),
  colors = c("red", "blue"),
  title = "Student Hangout"
)



# use icon scales, as with leaflet::addLegend()
icons <- c("temperature-low", "temperature-half", "temperature-high")
iconPal <- iconBin(icons, domain = 0:30, bins = 3, pretty = FALSE)
colorPal <- colorBin("RdYlBu", domain = 0:30, bins = 3, pretty = FALSE,
                     reverse = TRUE)

leaflet() |>
  addIconLegend(
    pal = iconPal,
    values = c(2, 15, 28),
    colors = colorPal,
    title = "Temperature",
    labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = "&deg;C")
  )
